archetype.name: Pocket Passer (accuracy-first)
archetype.definition: A 14th-year passer who wins with ball placement and on-time throws from the pocket, now with almost no rushing value left, and whose recurring weak spot is taking sacks rather than throwing errant balls.

report.headline: Accurate and turnover-free so far, but sacks and soft defenses inflate the picture
report.take:
Geno Smith at 36 is what he has been since his Seattle revival: an accurate pocket passer who puts the ball where it belongs. His 72.6% completion rate ranks 3rd of 42 qualifiers, his 4.3% bad-throw rate ranks 2nd of 32, and that is not a hot streak. He ranked 2nd, 3rd and 5th in bad-throw rate in 2022, 2024 and 2025. What is gone is the running. He is at -0.64 EPA per carry on 13 runs, both designed runs were stuffed, and his eight scrambles have lost value. The 2026 version is a 0.156 EPA-per-dropback rebound from a 2025 Raiders season that ranked 50th of 65 in EPA, with a league-worst 17 interceptions.

The efficiency rests on a thin layer of deep throws. His 12 attempts of 20+ air yards produced 3 TDs and 2.241 EPA apiece, roughly 27 points of value. His four game logs add up to about 20 points of passing EPA in total, so everything else he has done adds up to slightly below zero. The intermediate work (0.512 EPA on 17 throws) is good, the short game (0.127 on 68) is ordinary, and the 19 throws behind the line have lost value. A 36.3 CPOE on deep balls is not a repeatable number on 12 attempts.

Two more things sit under the surface. The first is sacks. He is pressured on only 18.3% of dropbacks (14th of 32), yet 39.1% of those pressures become sacks (30th). His time to throw has crept up to 2.94 seconds from the 2.80-2.84 range of his last four seasons. Eleven of his 12 sacks came in shotgun, six came on third down and three in the red zone, where drives die. This is a long-running trait (46.2% pressure-to-sack in 2025, 35.5% in 2024), not a new flaw. The second is the schedule. His two big games came against defenses now ranked 21st, 27th and 32nd. The one top-five unit he faced, Chicago, held him to 8-of-15 and -4.9 EPA. The zero interceptions also cut against a career in which he ranked 54th or worse in picks in three of the last four years.

From here the supporting cast thins. Breece Hall, Adonai Mitchell, Mason Taylor and guard Dylan Parham are all listed Out as of Oct. 5. Hall (0.854 EPA per target) and Mitchell (0.576) were two of his most efficient outlets, and Parham has played 86% of snaps. Expect the accuracy to hold. Expect the deep-ball efficiency and the zero in the interception column to come back toward his norms. That leaves a solid, ordinary starter: his career profile points to roughly 210-240 yards a game, with sacks as the tax.

strengths.title: Ball placement that holds every year
strengths.body: He completes passes well above expectation and almost never misses badly, ranking 3rd in completion rate and 2nd in bad-throw rate. His career shows top-five bad-throw rates in multiple seasons and top-ten CPOE in 2021, 2022 and 2024, so this is skill, not schedule. It should hold even as the receiving corps changes, because it is about where the ball goes, not who catches it.

strengths.title: Pushing it past the sticks pays
strengths.body: When he throws beyond 10 yards, the offense moves: 0.512 EPA on intermediate throws and 2.241 on deep shots with 3 TDs. He also works the middle (0.925 EPA on 16 throws) and the right side efficiently. The willingness to push it is real, with aggressiveness up to 17.95% from 12.5-15.4% in recent years. The deep efficiency on 12 attempts will shrink, but the intermediate game is a sustainable piece.

concerns.title: Pressures turn into sacks
concerns.body: He is not under siege, sitting mid-pack in pressure rate, but 39.1% of pressures end in sacks and his 9.3% sack rate ranks 35th of 42. His time to throw is up to 2.94 seconds, and the sacks cluster on third down and in the red zone, where they cost the most. His career shows this is a recurring trait, not a blip. With starting guard Parham out, it is more likely to persist than fade.

concerns.title: Efficiency built on soft defenses
concerns.body: His best game (321 yards, 3 TDs, 10.9 EPA) came against Detroit's defense, now ranked 32nd. Against Chicago's 5th-ranked unit he managed 119 yards and -4.9 EPA. Combine that with a 12-throw deep sample doing most of the lifting, and the 0.156 EPA per dropback looks inflated. A truer level is closer to his 0.07-0.085 seasons in Seattle.

concerns.title: Zero interceptions won't last
concerns.body: No interceptions on 117 attempts is the best in the league, but he threw 15 and 17 picks the last two seasons, ranking near the bottom both years. He already has three turnover-worthy fumbles, so ball security is not clean. Expect interceptions to return at something like his career rate. That will chip at both the efficiency numbers and the Jets' margin for error.

trend.note: He climbed from a tidy 215-yard opener through a 321-yard, 3-TD peak in Detroit, then fell to 119 yards on 15 attempts against Chicago. The swings line up closely with opponent quality and pass-rush pressure.

nextGame.headline: Generous to QBs on paper, but the pass rush tests his weakness
nextGame.body:
Cleveland's defense is middling by EPA (16th overall, 13th against the pass) but has been kind to quarterbacks: 261.5 passing yards (20th) and 2.25 TDs (26th) allowed per game, with an explosive-pass rate allowed that ranks 21st. That fits his strength of pushing the ball downfield. The problem is the rush. Cleveland's 7.5% sack rate ranks 9th, and he converts pressure to sacks at one of the worst rates in the league. Game script could also force volume. Cleveland passes more than any team relative to situation, and the Jets' pass defense ranks 23rd.

Availability tilts against him. Hall, Mitchell, tight end Mason Taylor and starting guard Parham are all listed Out as of Oct. 5. That leaves Garrett Wilson (32 targets), Kenyon Sadiq and Isaiah Williams as the main outlets and a patched interior line. On Cleveland's side, interior lineman Mason Graham is questionable with an MCL and ankle sprain, which would soften the inside rush if he sits. Starting center Elgton Jenkins (100% of snaps) is out, which hurts a Browns run game that already ranks 31st in EPA.

keyMatchups.title: Browns pass rush vs. sack-prone pocket
keyMatchups.body: Cleveland gets home at a top-ten rate, and his 39.1% pressure-to-sack rate means pressure is likely to end plays rather than produce throwaways. Parham's absence weakens the interior. Graham's knee and ankle status is the swing on the other side.

keyMatchups.title: A thinner target tree
keyMatchups.body: Losing Hall and Mitchell removes two of his most efficient targets per throw. Volume should concentrate on Wilson, who has handled 32 targets at 0.416 EPA each. The depth below him is unproven at this volume, which caps the ceiling more than the floor.

keyMatchups.title: Cleveland's pass-first script
keyMatchups.body: Cleveland leads the league in pass rate over expected, and its run game is nearly unusable, now without its starting center. If the Browns move it through the air against a Jets pass defense ranked 23rd, he will need to keep pace, which raises his attempt count from the 15 he threw in Chicago.

nextGame.watch: Whether he gets the ball out faster than his 2.94-second average on third down against Cleveland's rush. Sacks there decide whether drives finish.

restOfSeason.body:
The accuracy is the bankable part. Elite bad-throw rates and above-expectation completion have followed him for five seasons and should keep the floor respectable. What will regress is the deep-ball efficiency, built on 12 throws, and the zero interceptions, given his recent history. Expect his EPA per dropback to settle closer to the 0.07-0.09 range of his best Seattle years than the current 0.156.

The sacks are likely to stay a drag given his career pattern and the line injuries. With a 27th-ranked run game, the Jets will keep asking him to carry drives. That props up volume, and the returns of Hall, Mitchell and Taylor would matter more to his ceiling than anything in his own game. A useful mid-tier starter, not the top-ten passer the early efficiency ranking implies.

confidence.note: Four games and a 12-throw deep sample drive the efficiency.
